passage: Teacher's note, Class 11 project week. Written by Lokesh Sir. Shankar stayed back today and told me what he had noticed in his group of five. Meenal and Zubin had done almost all the research and the slides, while the other three, Shankar included until last week, kept saying, "We'll do it tomorrow." He said, "Sir, nobody's name is on any part, so nobody's responsible. The two careful ones end up doing everything, and today Meenal snapped at all of us." He said he felt bad about his own part. I have changed the project sheet: each member now signs for a named section, and there is a short check-in every Thursday. Shankar asked to take the data section.

qa.q: How many students were in Shankar's group?
qa.a: Five.

qa.q: Why did Shankar feel bad when he spoke to Lokesh Sir?
qa.a: He felt guilty, having been one of the three putting work off until last week, so he felt partly responsible for Meenal and Zubin carrying the load.

qa.q: What did Lokesh Sir change, and why should it help?
qa.a: Each member now signs for a named section with a Thursday check-in, so everyone is accountable and the careful two no longer carry everything.

qa.q: What might Meenal's snapping reveal about how Meenal felt?
qa.a: Meenal likely felt resentful and worn out after doing most of the research and slides while others kept postponing.

grounding: A student recognises that with no one accountable in a group project, two careful members carry the work and grow resentful, and the teacher adds named roles.

passage: Thursday. I'm one of the four boys in our geography project group, and today I finally saw what's been going on. Chinmay and Esther have done everything: the map, the report, the model of the river. The rest of us "helped" by sending thumbs-up in the group chat. Today Esther stayed back till six gluing labels while Abel and Sunny went to play football. Nobody is in charge of anything, so nobody feels guilty. Chinmay didn't complain, but when Sunny said, "Great work, team!" he went very quiet and packed up without saying bye. I think he's fed up. Honestly, I would be. Tomorrow I'm taking the labels home and doing the river section myself. And I'm going to suggest we each put our name on one part. - Thomas

qa.q: Until what time did Esther stay back?
qa.a: Till six.

qa.q: What does Chinmay packing up without saying bye suggest he felt?
qa.a: He seemed fed up and resentful that Esther and he did everything while the others shared the credit.

qa.q: What two choices does Thomas make for tomorrow, and why do they matter?
qa.a: Taking the labels home and doing the river section, and suggesting each person names one part, so the load is shared and everyone is accountable.

qa.q: How might Esther feel hearing 'Great work, team!'?
qa.a: Esther may feel irritated, since the team credit covered work that Esther and Chinmay mostly did.

grounding: A boy notices that in his group, with nobody accountable, two careful members carry the project and start to resent it, and he decides to change his part.

passage: In the government school at Sironj, the Class 10 science project was to test water from four village hand pumps. Gopal, fifteen, was in the group of six. From the back bench he watched it happen week after week. Payal walked to the pumps with bottles after school. Vandana wrote up every result in her neat hand. The other four, Gopal among them, said, "Tell us what to do," and then went to the tea stall. Nobody had a named job, so nobody felt it was theirs. On Friday Vandana slammed the file on the desk. "We are not your servants." Payal did not say anything, but she did not smile all day. Gopal saw it then: the careful ones had carried everything, and now they were fed up.

qa.q: Who wrote up every result for the project?
qa.a: Vandana wrote up every result in her neat hand.

qa.q: What does Gopal realise on Friday, and how might it feel?
qa.a: Gopal likely feels uncomfortable and a little ashamed, seeing that the careful ones carried everything and that Gopal was one of those who went to the tea stall.

qa.q: What choice could Gopal make now that he has seen the problem?
qa.a: He could ask the group to give each person a named job, and take one of the pump visits or write-ups himself.

qa.q: How does Payal seem to feel by Friday, and what shows it?
qa.a: She seems quietly hurt and tired of carrying the work, because she stays silent and does not smile all day.

grounding: A teenage boy watches his group leave the project to two diligent girls and sees how having no named jobs leaves them carrying the load and resenting it.

passage: In their school in Porto Alegre, the science-fair team had five names on the sign-up sheet. Emil, sixteen, noticed who actually stayed after the bell. Priscila, every day, rewiring the little wind turbine. Tomás, cutting blades out of plastic bottles. The other three, Emil included, kept saying, "Message us if you need anything," and walked out. On Wednesday the turbine would not spin. Priscila stayed until the caretaker switched off the lights. The next morning Emil heard her tell Tomás, "If our names are on it, why is it only us?" Tomás only shrugged and rubbed his eyes, looking worn out. Emil thought about the sign-up sheet in his bag. Five names, but no one was down for any single job, so three of them could vanish and nobody would notice. Except those two.

qa.q: What were Priscila and Tomás making for the science fair?
qa.a: They were building a little wind turbine, with Priscila rewiring it and Tomás cutting blades out of plastic bottles.

qa.q: What was Priscila feeling when she spoke to Tomás the next morning?
qa.a: She was frustrated and resentful, asking why only the two of them did the work when all five names were on the project.

qa.q: What could Emil do with what he has noticed?
qa.a: He could suggest writing one job next to each name on the sheet and take on a real part of the turbine himself instead of just offering to help by message.

qa.q: How does the situation look from Tomás's side?
qa.a: He is worn out from doing the work while others leave, and his tired shrug suggests he has stopped expecting the others to help.

grounding: A teenage boy observes that when no one has a named job, two careful teammates carry the whole project and grow resentful.
